The main progress in this area is attributed to the implementation of multimode systems based on squeezed states of light. One of the simplest ways to generate such states relies upon their producing in a single-pass optical parametric amplifier (OPA) under ultrafast pumping. However, for homodyne detection of such multimode states, the profile of the local oscillator (LO) must perfectly match the profile of the measured mode. Usually, this is not the case; therefore, a proper treatment of multimode squeezing is required. In this work, we study both theoretically and experimentally the multimode squeezed light generated in type-0 and type-II OPA. We characterize such sources using the Schmidt-mode representation and investigate the degree of squeezing depending on the LO spectral profile, employing a pulse shaping technique. In addition, we investigate cluster states that can be generated under the given experimental conditions. This work might have a significant impact on the realization of multimode quantum protocols.

papers.title: AgentGrad: Intervention-guided Prompt Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) achieve strong performance by employing specialized multiple agents, yet their performance depends on the prompt design of each agent. For MAS prompt optimization, textual gradient methods that guide prompt updates using natural-language feedback have emerged as a leading paradigm. In this paper, we identify limitations in two stages of existing textual gradient approaches: gradient extraction and gradient aggregation. In gradient extraction, previous works select a prompt to update without verifying whether modifying it resolves the failure, and derive gradients without agent-level supervision over the corresponding agent's intermediate output. In gradient aggregation, individual gradients are randomly grouped and concatenated, often mixing unrelated failure modes and producing prompts that fail to generalize. To address these limitations, we propose AgentGrad, a prompt optimization framework for multi-agent systems based on sequential intervention and semantic textual gradient abstraction. For each failure, sequential intervention injects a hint into one agent at a time to identify the target agent whose modification resolves the failure. The modified output of the target agent then serves as agent-level supervision for extracting a fine-grained gradient. Semantic textual gradient abstraction clusters semantically similar gradients to prevent mixing unrelated failure modes, and abstracts each cluster into a generalized gradient that captures the shared corrective pattern. Experimental results show that AgentGrad achieves state-of-the-art performance across five MAS benchmarks while reducing wall-clock optimization time by 2.5 times and optimization cost by 21.8% on average compared to the next-best baselines. Our code is available at https://github.com/mlvlab/AgentGrad.

papers.title: Multi-bounce Drum Roll with Optimized Active Tricks to Leverage Soft Embodiment
papers.abstract: This paper presents a soft robotic drummer for accurate and efficient drum rolls. High-frequency drum rolls require the "multi-bounce technique," where a drumstick bounces multiple times with a single stroke. In robotic reproduction of this technique, the body's elasticity is key, while the fine motion during the stroke is also crucial for maximizing the potential of that elasticity. Therefore, we design two tricks: i) Tap-Pull (TP) trick to increase the number of rebounds by adding a pulling motion after impact; and ii) Micro-Pulse (MP) trick to keep the drumming volume by injecting small oscillations during the stroke. Due to the nonlinear complexity of soft embodiment, both tricks are efficiently tuned using Bayesian optimization in a data-driven manner for accomplishing the respective objectives quantified. We evaluated the optimized behaviors with soft and rigid end-effectors. As a result, the soft TP achieved the highest bounce count (12.25 per stroke) with uniform intervals. The soft MP suppressed the volume decay, yielding 6.8-times higher acoustic efficiency compared to the rigid MP. These results indicate that the proposed tricks with the combination of elasticity and optimization can make robots play excellent drum rolls.

papers.title: Robust and Sparse Group Dynamic Causal Modeling via Student-t Parametric Empirical Bayes and Nonlocal Priors
papers.abstract: Dynamic causal modeling (DCM) estimates directed effective connectivity, while parametric empirical Bayes (PEB) supports group inference using subject-specific posterior summaries. Standard PEB relies on Gaussian models and continuous shrinkage, making it sensitive to atypical estimates and unable to distinguish negligible from nonzero effects. We develop a robust and sparse group-DCM extension combining a Student-$t$ likelihood with a spike-and-slab prior using a nonlocal product-moment (pMOM) slab. A normal--gamma representation of the Student-$t$ distribution yields weights that downweight atypical {whitened residual coordinates}. The pMOM slab vanishes at zero, sharpening coefficient selection and yielding inclusion probabilities. {We propagate first-level posterior uncertainty through block-covariance pre-whitening and use a multistart generalized expectation--maximization (EM) algorithm with conditional maximization for mode fitting, followed by parallel-tempering posterior integration for inclusion probabilities. A simulation study showed that Student-$t$ weighting supplied the main protection against contamination, while spike-and-slab regularization reduced fixed-threshold false selections. In an openly shared mixed-gambles fMRI application, we found mild heterogeneity, concentrated inclusion support on departures of all four diagonal self-inhibition scaling parameters from the SPM default, and close directional agreement with standard PEB implemented in Statistical Parametric Mapping.} Our framework therefore adds interpretable {whitened-coordinate} robustness diagnostics and sparse coefficient selection to hierarchical DCM while retaining first-level uncertainty.

papers.title: Vertex interpolation by bivariate $C^1$ cubic splines: counterexamples, geometric stability, and indecomposable defects
papers.abstract: We study vertex evaluation on the full space of continuously differentiable piecewise cubic polynomials on a fixed planar triangulation. A complete dual description turns failure of interpolation into balanced edge weights with nonzero vertex loading. It leads to exact counterexamples with 17, 25, 31 and 41 vertices, each with one relation and the classical lower-bound dimension. The 31- and 41-vertex examples have interior graphs that are trees. We give a geometric construction criterion for a sector-completion family and a certified implicit construction outside that family. With all boundary vertices fixed, the nearby bad configurations form a four-dimensional smooth locus in the 17-vertex case, two intersecting components of dimensions six and five in the 25-vertex case, and isolated transverse points in the two tree examples. A common Schur-complement estimate explains their different interpolation costs. We first realize arbitrary defect by decomposable chains of the 41-vertex example. We then construct obstructions from individually interpolatory blocks, prove that the capacity of one complete edge is exactly five, and build a fixed-square family with arbitrarily large strongly indecomposable defect. The latter excludes two triangle-disjoint connected normal bad submeshes even when those submeshes may have holes.

papers.title: A Wavelength Borrowing Architecture for Optical Data Center Networks - Extended Version
papers.abstract: The growth of east-west traffic, along with the cost and power consumption of electronic switching, is motivating the integration of a low-power, high-rate, all-optical layer within the data center network. This paper presents a spine-leaf all-optical architecture in which the default wavelength configuration, one wavelength per source--destination leaf pair, can be reconfigured to accommodate unbalanced traffic demand: wavelengths that are unused or lightly loaded at one leaf are borrowed by another leaf with higher demand. This topology-engineering capability is combined with a traffic-engineering scheme, based on two-hop detouring, enabling the control of wavelength load while limiting the amount of detoured traffic. A key feature of the architecture is that its degree of wavelength reconfigurability is set by a single tunable parameter, the borrowing degree $B$, ranging from none to full; performance evaluation shows that performance nearly equal to that of a fully reconfigurable architecture is achieved well below the maximum $B$, saving the complexity of a fully reconfigurable solutions. The optical fabric relies on mature, data-center-grade components, namely AWGs, AWGRs, colorless OXCs, and combiners. The reconfiguration speed and the adopted dynamic control policy make the architecture suitable for network tiers where the traffic varies on timescales of tens of minutes or more, e.g., among groups of racks (pods).

papers.title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Major open-source serving stacks reuse the key-value tensors of a shared prefix by default. We measure what this prefix reuse costs in reproducibility. Holding model, decoding, seed and request order fixed at batch size one, we ran an eighty-episode multi-turn agentic tool-use workload with prefix reuse on and off across two engines and four weight formats. Without prefix reuse, repeated runs reproduced every token and log-probability in all ten configurations. With it, cache-hit and recompute paths diverged on both engines. On llama.cpp with GGUF weights this path divergence rises with quantization: for Qwen2.5-7B over ten independent server histories, it reached 37.4 percent of episodes at 16-bit and 82.5 percent at four-bit. Near-tie decisions became only about 1.2 times as common, while the cache-path change in top-two margins grew 4.9-fold from 16-bit to three-bit. Serving four-bit weights through 16-bit kernels left divergence not detectably different from 16-bit, placing the amplification mainly in the quantized execution path. At Q4_K_M, run-to-run divergence came mainly from llama.cpp's server-level prompt cache: under the canonical episode order it moved divergence by 37.5 points, and at its default, divergence spanned 20.0 to 28.7 percent under five random orders. With cache state restored, each path reproduced exactly while the two still differed. In the tested stacks, cached serving is irreproducible because the cache state is absent from the request and not reset by default. A single-turn bridge shows path divergence reaching task outcomes with no detectable net change in accuracy. We release the harness, logs, and analysis pipeline.

papers.title: Optimizing Credential Blast Radius Through Trust Boundaries and Delegation Under Post-Quantum Authentication Costs
papers.abstract: Partitioning interacting services into independently rooted trust domains limits issuer-compromise reach while increasing calls across trust boundaries. Post-quantum replacements for public-key authentication and key-establishment mechanisms can increase crossing latency on constrained or lossy paths. We formulate the joint selection of trust domains and credential-derivation structures under policy and latency constraints, linking separate service-interaction and credential-derivation graphs through domain assignment. Credential blast radius measures weighted service impact after compromise. A linear upper bound supports optimization, while a joint event model gives exact expected impact. We identify when risk from issuers trusted across domains can be incorporated into this linear score, avoiding separate issuer-propagation calculations for each candidate. Although the general problem is NP-hard, we identify restricted cases that can be solved efficiently and exactly. Joint optimization yields lower blast radius than choosing boundaries first in 195 of 230 exhaustive synthetic comparisons, especially under chained delegation. A trace-derived replay used measured post-quantum costs, synthetic risk inputs, a fixed derivation family, and one to six trust domains. Under independent compromise events, mean expected impact was up to 36% lower than with one domain within the latency budget. The framework turns risk assumptions and measured crossing costs into candidate trust-domain and credential-derivation designs.

papers.title: Wormhole-induced gravi-axion mass distributions and the second-harmonic crossover
papers.abstract: We compute the distribution of the wormhole-induced gravi-axion curvature mass across baby-universe sectors when the first two harmonics are retained. For independent complex Gaussian coefficients, with an optional displacement of the first channel, an exact global-minimum condition gives the mass distribution and its threshold coefficient. At fixed nonzero second-harmonic width, the cumulative probability below mass $M$ scales as $M^5$. For a weak second harmonic, the unit-harmonic $M^4$ behavior is recovered in an intermediate low-mass range above the crossover scale. We also distinguish the actual relative mass-squared error from the probability that a phase-independent bound fails to certify the unit-harmonic approximation. In the common-background quadratic correlator with unit residues, the lower threshold remains zero and the two-harmonic tail produces an $s^{3/2}$ nonanalytic term in the Euclidean momentum squared $s$. The results are conditional on the chosen state and effective wormhole coefficients.

papers.title: Rapid Growth of Intermediate-Mass Black Holes through Disk-induced Stellar Disruptions
papers.abstract: Dense nuclear star clusters provide unique environments for studying the dynamical interactions between stars and massive black holes. When an accretion disk is present, dissipative star--disk interactions can capture surrounding stars, drive their inward migration, and ultimately lead to disk-induced tidal disruption events\,(dTDEs). The long-term feeding rate from this process, however, cannot be inferred from single-orbit migration estimates alone, as it depends on the coupled evolution of disk capture, collisional relaxation, stellar depletion and replenishment, and physical mergers within the star cluster. In this work, we use high-performance direct $N$-body simulations combined with analytic prescriptions for star--disk interactions to follow this coupled evolution for intermediate-mass black holes\,(IMBHs) with accretion disks embedded in dense stellar clusters. The simulations track the formation of the stellar cusp, the capture of stars by repeated disk crossings, their subsequent orbital damping and migration, and their eventual consumption by the central IMBH. We find that dTDEs can sustain stellar mass supply rates of $\sim10^{-3}\,M_\odot \,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which exceeds the Eddington-limited gas accretion rate for IMBHs with $M_\bullet 30$ Myr.

papers.title: Exemplar: Few-Shot Biomedical Segmentation That Fits in Seconds
papers.abstract: Segmenting a new microscopy dataset usually means training a deep network on its annotations, and training again for every added image. Exemplar solves a segmentation readout in closed form and updates it exactly with each new mask in seconds, as accurately as networks trained for minutes. The updated readout is identical to a fit from all masks at once. Its linear readout combines frozen DINOv3 features, read at a magnification chosen from the masks, with classical filter responses at native resolution. Its regularisation and its pixel weighting are chosen exactly by leaving out one annotated image at a time, so none is set aside for validation. On ten biomedical datasets from cells to vessels and filaments, Exemplar is more accurate than every few-shot method that only applies a pretrained model, and on average than nnU-Net trained on the same masks. A fine-tuned Cellpose-SAM, the strongest baseline, is as accurate on average, but each of its fits takes a median of 25 minutes against 8.5 seconds, and each new mask means fine-tuning it again.

papers.title: Liquid-liquid phase transitions in dipolar liquids. Insights into Supercooled Water
papers.abstract: Dipolar liquids combine two coupled degrees of freedom, translational and dipolar. Intriguingly, these two sectors can reside in distinct thermodynamic states, with the state of one sector possibly favouring a specific state of the other. The onset of ferroelectric order in dipolar liquids is an example of this mutual stabilization. Since this coupling is often encoded in interaction potentials, projecting out one sector to derive an effective interaction for the other can uncover the microscopic mechanism underlying this phenomenon. A coarse-grained theory, solved in the large-dimensional limit, in which the distance between nearest-neighbour particles depends on their dipolar interaction through a density-dependent mechanical compliance shows that a ferroelectric transition can trigger a liquid-liquid transition. It also predicts a first-order liquid-liquid transition within the paraelectric phase that, in turn, can promote ferroelectric ordering. The anisotropic dipolar-dependent soft-core interaction is shown to lead to an effective Jagla-like isotropic two-length-scale interaction, known to support liquid-liquid phase transitions. Here, however, the two-length-scale pattern depends on density and dipolar configuration, and is therefore sensitive to dipolar order. Analysis of supercooled TIP4P/Ice water molecular dynamics simulations shows that first-coordination-shell features of the pair correlation functions are sensitive to dipolar interaction, supporting the foundations of the coarse-grained theory. Comparison of low- and high-density liquid water reveals enhanced spatial anisotropy of the first coordination shell in the low-density liquid, associated, within the theory, with increased effective excluded volume, showing that the liquid-liquid transition involves structural changes within the first shell, beyond reorganization of the interstitial region and tetrahedral order.

papers.title: Resolvent Estimates for the Stokes Operator in a Three-Dimensional Lipschitz Domain
papers.abstract: By refining the approach developed in \cite{AGH-2015, GS2026a}, we establish resolvent estimates in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$ for the Stokes operator in a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ in $\R^3$ for $(3/2)-\e 0$ depends on $\Omega$. As a consequence, the Stokes operator generates a uniformly bounded analytic semigroup in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$. The range for $p$ is sharp. The results are particularly surprising, as it is long believed that the $L^p$ resolvent estimates in three-dimensional Lipschitz domains may fail for large $p$. In the appendices we prove an interpolation theorem between $L^2_\sigma(\Omega)$ and $L^\infty_\sigma(\Omega)$. We also show that for $1< p< \infty$ and a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ in $\R^d, d\ge 2$, the resolvent estimate in $L^p(\Omega; \C^d)$ can hold only if the Helmholtz projection is bounded on this space. This explains the counter-example constructed in \cite{Deuring-2001}. Finally, we prove that the resolvent estimate may fail in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$ for $1< p< (3/2)$ and $d\ge 3$ as a consequence of failure of the Helmholtz decomposition of $L^p(\Omega; \C^d)$.

papers.title: The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial: A Subgroup-Lattice Refinement
papers.abstract: We introduce the multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomial F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{h\in H}P_{\Gamma/h}(x,y), which aggregates the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials associated with all subgroups of a finite group acting on a graph. We derive the equivalent element-wise representation F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{g\in G}c_G(g)P_{\Gamma/g}(x,y), where c_G(g) = \sum_{\langle g\rangle\leq H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}. The coefficient function depends only on the cyclic subgroup generated by the element and is constant on conjugacy classes. This yields decompositions by cyclic subgroups and conjugacy classes and an interpretation in terms of the incidence algebra of the subgroup lattice. After normalization, the coefficients define a probability distribution obtained by choosing a subgroup uniformly and then an element uniformly from that subgroup. We also establish diagonal multiplicativity for disjoint unions and a weighted cycle-index expression for edgeless graphs. A further contribution concerns the distinguishing power of the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial. We answer a question of Dohmen and Lange-Geisler affirmatively by exhibiting two non-isomorphic graphs, P_3 and K_2 \mathbin{\dot\cup} K_1 under C_2-actions, with identical orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. The two actions nevertheless have different multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. Thus the multiorbital polynomial is not determined by the orbital bivariate polynomial, whereas the converse question remains open.

papers.title: Amortized Opacity Marginalization Improves C/O Interval Calibration for Brown-Dwarf Retrievals
papers.abstract: Molecular line lists disagree at a level that measurably shifts retrieved C/O, so retrievals conditioned on a single list omit a dominant systematic from their error bars. Classical marginalization re-runs a full retrieval under K opacity realizations per object. We move that cost into simulation: while generating the training set we randomize opacities (smooth multiplicative Fourier fields in log(nu) plus a discrete line-list mixture, under a deliberately broad prior informed by measured inter-list differences), so a neural posterior estimator learns an already-marginalized posterior. On perturbed held-out spectra (n=2048) a standard NPE covers nominal 90% C/O intervals 43.3% of the time against 82.4% for a compute-matched marginalized network; three-seed control ensembles reach 93.2% on clean data but 61.4% under perturbation, against 89.4% marginalized, isolating the deficit as opacity-induced (TARP joint expected-coverage deviation 0.005 against 0.035 for a single control network). An axis ablation traces the gain to the continuous field (45.4% for the discrete swaps alone, 79.3% for the field alone). In simulation, real JWST bad-pixel masks with median filling cut the marginalized ensemble's C/O coverage from 0.894 to 0.683; an ensemble retrained with mask augmentation holds 0.918 under the full deployment preprocessing (n=1024). We apply the networks to one pipeline-combined JWST/NIRSpec G395H spectrum each of 14 late-T and Y dwarfs. The recommended mask-augmented ensemble returns C/O medians between 0.24 and 0.62 and contains the Hood et al. (2024) value of 0.53 for the T8 benchmark 2MASS J0415-0935, which every fixed-opacity control network excludes. With 90% intervals spanning about 0.43 of the prior width, this is a consistency check, not a validation.

papers.title: The Greedy Superstring Conjecture Is False
papers.abstract: In the Shortest Common Superstring problem (SCS), one is given a finite set of strings and is asked to find a shortest string containing every input string as a substring. Since the problem is NP-hard, various approximation algorithms have been proposed for it. The currently best known approximation ratio is $2.466$ due to Englert, Matsakis, and Vesel\'y; a better approximation ratio $2$ has been announced by OpenAI just recently. In 1988, Tarhio and Ukkonen introduced a simple greedy algorithm that iteratively takes two strings with the longest overlap and merges them together. They showed that the greedy algorithm may produce a superstring that is about two times longer than the optimal one and conjectured that this bound is tight. This has become known as the Greedy Superstring Conjecture and has remained open for almost four decades. The best known upper bound on the approximation ratio of the greedy algorithm is $3.396$ due to Englert, Matsakis, and Vesel\'y. In this paper, we present a series of results tightening the bounds of the greedy algorithm, with the main contributions being as follows: 1. We refute the Greedy Conjecture by constructing a family of instances for which a lower bound on the approximation ratio tends to $2.4$. 2. We prove that the greedy algorithm is $3$-approximate. 3. For input strings of fixed length $k$, we prove that the approximation guarantee is exactly $9/5$ for $k=3$ and at least $2$ for all $k \ge 6$.

papers.title: Narrow-Sense Type-III Dirac Cones and Additional Flat Lines on a Honeycomb Lattice with Anisotropic Next-Nearest-Neighbor Hoppings
papers.abstract: Critically tilted Dirac cones have attracted considerable attention because of their unconventional electronic properties in two-dimensional massless Dirac-fermion systems. Among them, the narrow-sense type-III Dirac cone is characterized by a flat dispersion along the direction connecting the two Dirac points. Using a tight-binding model on a single-orbital honeycomb lattice, we demonstrate that narrow-sense type-III Dirac cones can be realized by tuning anisotropic next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. Type-I and type-II Dirac cones emerge on either side of the critical point, enabling a systematic investigation of the electronic properties across the type-I, narrow-sense type-III, and type-II regimes. We further find that the present model exhibits additional flat lines in momentum space whose energy coincides with the Dirac-point energy at the narrow-sense type-III critical point. These flat lines lead to a pronounced enhancement of the density of states above the Fermi energy and, consequently, the electronic specific heat is substantially enhanced compared with that expected for an ideal narrow-sense type-III Dirac cone. Our results show that the honeycomb lattice with anisotropic next-nearest-neighbor hoppings provides a simple platform for exploring unconventional thermodynamic properties arising from the energy coincidence of narrow-sense type-III Dirac cones and additional flat lines at the Fermi energy.

papers.title: Beyond Landmark Extraction: A Framework for Robust Geometric Feature Evaluation in Structured Image Classification
papers.abstract: Much of the literature on structured image recognition has disproportionately focused on the comparison of classification algorithms. Rather than investigating which classifier performs best, this paper instead asks: what should a classifier know before it ever makes a prediction? In structured vision problems such as gesture recognition, facial expression categorization, and medical image analysis, discriminative information lies less in individual pixels and more in spatial relationships between semantic parts. Raw pixel spaces are high-dimensional, sensitive to nuisance variation, and often obfuscate the geometric structures that make visual tasks interpretable. Landmark extraction provides one form of dimension reduction, but it does not by itself determine the information preserved. This paper studies the post-landmark feature map as the central object of analysis and proposes a systematic framework for constructing and interpreting landmark-derived representations as an, informed, feature-based "dimension reduction" step. Using static hand gesture recognition as a case study, we evaluate coordinate, distance, angle, and hybrid representations through perturbation and ablation experiments. The results show that visually variable data exposes substantial gaps between raw coordinate features and their geometrically invariant counterparts, while hybrid representations achieve the strongest overall performance by combining complementary geometric components. These findings frame feature construction as a fundamental modeling decision and ultimately suggests that the question of what representation should a classifier learn from is one worth asking. The code used for feature construction and evaluation is available at https://github.com/ShivMaureeCWRU/Feature_based_dimension_reduction

papers.title: GenScale: A Benchmark for Relative Object Scale in Image Generation and Editing
papers.abstract: Modern image generation and editing systems can produce photorealistic, prompt-aligned images, but still often render familiar objects at implausible relative sizes. To measure this failure mode, we introduce GenScale, a benchmark and evaluation protocol for real-world relative object scale in image generation and editing. GenScale contains 900 image-level entries and 1,643 pairwise anchor-target scale relations across common-object generation, human-product generation with metric dimensions, and scale correction from failed generations. We further design a human-calibrated ordinal judge for scalable pairwise scale evaluation. Last but not least, we introduce Rescale, a model-agnostic post-processing agent for localized scale correction without modifying the source generator. Experiments reveal that state-of-the-art image generators and editors do not reliably render plausible relative scale, while Rescale consistently improves scale plausibility across generated and edited images. Together, GenScale establishes relative object scale as a distinct, measurable, and actionable capability for image generation systems.

papers.title: Multiple ergodic averages for commuting multiplicative actions
papers.abstract: We study the convergence of multiple ergodic averages involving several commuting multiplicative actions. We prove that for finitely generated systems, the averages $$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N S_{1,n}F_1\cdot\ldots\cdot S_{\ell,n}F_\ell$$ converge in norm, settling a conjecture of Frantzikinakis. Our proofs feature tools from ergodic theory and probabilistic number theory. We exploit some stability properties of additive functions to establish a novel variant of \Katai's orthogonality criterion, which leads to box seminorm control for our averages. Using the theory of magic extensions introduced by Host and a delicate complexity reduction argument, we eventually reduce our problem to known convergence results.

papers.title: Bounded Relative Boundary Implies Narrow DNF Approximation
papers.abstract: We prove Friedgut's conjecture (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999)) that every increasing family in the $p$-biased discrete cube with bounded relative boundary can be approximated arbitrarily well by one whose minimal elements have size bounded independently of the dimension and the bias. For $0<p\le 1/2$, every increasing Boolean function with total resampling influence at most $K$ is $\varepsilon$-close under $\mu_p^n$ to a monotone DNF of width $\exp(O((K+1)^2/\varepsilon^2))$, from which the full conjecture follows for all $p\in(0,1)$. We build on Hatami's pseudo-junta theorem (Ann. of Math. 176 (2012)), whose approximator need not be increasing. Our randomized shifts produce an increasing approximator that is measurable with respect to a controlled refinement of Hatami's adaptive partition. Retaining only short positive certificates yields the desired narrow DNF.

papers.title: A Dichotomy for Complex Boolean Holant with Binary Disequality
papers.abstract: We classify Boolean Holant problems with a supplied binary disequality signature and an arbitrary fixed finite set of algebraic complex-valued signatures. Each problem is polynomial-time computable or $\#\mathsf{P}$-hard, and the tractability criterion is decidable. The proof combines arity reduction with the growth of the available binary transfer group and uses stable pairs to recover the structure of higher-arity signatures. We also prove a dichotomy for the disequality-edge model when the signature set contains an endpoint-nondegenerate irreducible eight-vertex signature, resolving the corresponding arity-four cases in the main proof.

papers.title: BiG-SURE - Bipartite Graph for Semantic Uncertainty and Reliability Estimation of LLMs
papers.abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimation is a crucial requirement for deploying large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) in safety-critical settings, especially when the model parameters are not accessible (black-box). We propose BiG-SURE, an uncertainty estimator based on cross-temperature semantic agreement. The method samples low-temperature responses as stable semantic anchors and high-temperature responses as probes under meaning-preserving input transformations. It then constructs an anchor-probe Bipartite Graph (BiG) using NLI-based entailment scores and defines confidence through the normalized squared spectral energy of this matrix, with uncertainty given by its complement. This bipartite graph-based Semantic Uncertainty and Reliability Estimation (SURE) score measures whether high-temperature probes remain semantically aligned with the model's stable low-temperature belief or not. We evaluate BiG-SURE on text QA, multilingual QA, and multimodal QA tasks across multiple model families. In these experiments, BiG-SURE improves average abstention AUROC over prior black-box uncertainty estimators, while remaining simple, unsupervised, and applicable to black-box model settings.

papers.title: Best Annealing Path of Simulated Quantum Annealing via Efficient Adiabatic Phase Transition
papers.abstract: Nested Simulated Annealing (NSA) is proposed for accelerating the classical simulation of Quantum Annealing (QA). NSA is based on two-spin interaction and exploits the causality of spin-flip, thereby significantly reducing computational cost. And through Unitary Coupled-Cluster (UCC) method, I establish a connection between NSA and XX interaction which is one of non-stoquastic Hamiltonians and demonstrate that NSA effectively utilizes a trivial degenerate state. Furthermore, by treating spins as continuous variables, I derive an energy formulation that incorporates both the problem Hamiltonian and the perturbation Hamiltonian induced by transverse electromagnetic field and show that the annealing path characterized by the lowest local-maximum exhibits the fastest convergence. Based on the result, I present a strategy for finding optimal annealing parameters for Simulated Quantum Annealing (SQA).

papers.title: Robust Model Order Selection via Dithered Differential Step-Down Thresholding
papers.abstract: We propose a dithered differential step-down thresholding (DSDT) algorithm for robust model order selection in stationary noise. Evaluating only exceedance counts over a decreasing threshold grid, the proposed algorithm stops when detecting noise extrema value clustering. We prove that deterministic threshold grids are inconsistent under lowered floor detection thresholds due to threshold grid misalignment error. We bound this error using randomized grid dithering. For arbitrary deterministic shifts, any joint noise distribution, and data-dependent thresholds, we obtain non-asymptotic bounds on the estimation risk and family-wise error rate, establishing DSDT as a universal false alarm suppressor for any single-threshold algorithm. When the scale sequence tends to zero or extremes cluster along the search grid, DSDT achieves asymptotic exact order recovery of separated deterministic components exceeding the noise maximum plus the grid step, even below the minimax threshold or without a detection threshold. Using multiple independent dithers reduces error bounds. We provide convergence and consistency analysis for an arbitrary number of dithers. This analysis establishes asymptotic bounds under extreme value laws and non-asymptotic bounds under nondecreasing hazard rates. The results extend to unseparated deterministic shifts, random shifts, unknown noise scales, and multi-dimensional search grids. We show that DSDT is robust to data quantization.

papers.title: Portfolio Risk Bounds without Cross-Asset Return Covariances: Distributional Fields from Language-Model Representations
papers.abstract: Portfolio risk assessment ordinarily relies on reliable estimates of cross-asset return covariances, which are difficult to obtain in short, high-dimensional panels. We show that firm-level distribution-valued characteristics can instead provide one-sided certificates of portfolio risk. Under maintained links from characteristics to systematic exposures and from exposures to returns, multi-firm Wasserstein-2 dispersion yields a sharp upper bound on systematic portfolio variance and a corresponding bound for standardized returns. A weighted pairwise relaxation produces an objective that is convex under a checkable condition and requires marginal volatility scales but no cross-asset return covariances. With zero firm-specific slack, the common-map scale changes the certified variance reduction but not the normalized allocation, which depends only on observed information geometry. In a 100-firm panel from 2018-2022, only 0.09%-0.46% of portfolios across four prespecified capped reference populations have in-sample variance no greater than an allocation constructed from Qwen3-Embedding-8B news representations; the corresponding share for equal risk weighting is 28.3%-34.7%. The lower in-sample variance ranking relative to equal risk also appears across the reported frozen language-model representations. The framework therefore converts distribution-valued firm information into a coherent risk bound and an implementable allocation rule constructed without cross-asset return covariances.

papers.title: Who Are a Firm's Economic Peers? Mapping a Latent Information Field with Language Models
papers.abstract: Identifying a firm's economic peers matters for benchmarking, risk measurement, and understanding return dependence, yet a diversified firm may have no single natural peer. We use language-model representations of corporate news to identify the combination of firms that jointly represents each firm's information environment. Each firm is represented by a distribution of article embeddings, and target-anchored Wasserstein barycentric reconstruction produces a directed map of economic-peer weights. We use this map as the interaction structure in a spatial factor model and ask whether return dependence follows peer relations measured from news without using returns. We construct peer weights from 2018-2022 news for 100 large-cap US traded firms and evaluate their financial relevance in subsequent returns. Relative to a matched model with the Fama-French five factors and momentum, the information field firms' unexpected returns move together after common factor exposures are accounted for. Joint reconstruction contributes substantially more than pairwise Wasserstein proximity or equal weighting of the selected peers, while centroid reconstruction retains most of the gain. Explicit news co-mentions provide complementary information. Language models thus make the interaction structure in spatial asset pricing an object of measurement: economically interpretable peer relations can be constructed from text before their financial relevance is assessed in returns.

papers.title: Probability-based Estimates of the Uncalculated N$^5$LO QCD Contribution to the Hadronic $W$-Boson Decay Width
papers.abstract: The perturbative QCD corrections to the hadronic decay width of the $W$ boson are currently known up to next-to-next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order ($\mathrm{N^4LO}$), whereas the exact $\mathrm{N^5LO}$ correction remains unavailable owing to its formidable computational complexity. In this work, we estimate the $\mathrm{N^5LO}$ contributions by adopting Bayesian analysis (BA). Before performing the estimation, the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) is employed to improve the precision of the initial scale-dependent perturbative series. Through recursive application of the renormalization group equation, non-conformal terms are absorbed into the strong running coupling, yielding a scheme-independent, scale-invariant perturbative series with improved convergence. The PMC procedure determines an effective coupling $\alpha_s(Q_*)$, with the PMC scale fixed as $Q_* = 100.102~\mathrm{GeV}$ at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy. Based on the improved and more precise series, the $95.5\%$ BA credible interval yields an uncertainty of $\Delta\delta_\mathrm{QCD}|_{\mathrm{PMC, BA}}^{\mathrm{N^5LO}} = \pm 1.0\times 10^{-5}$. The resulting hadronic branching ratio is $\mathcal{B}(W\to \text{hadrons})|_\mathrm{PMC} = (65.84\pm 1.54)\%$, which is consistent with experimental data within reasonable errors.

papers.title: Benchmark Contamination: A Taxonomy Organized by Defeated Mitigation
papers.abstract: A benchmark score is a joint property of the model, the evaluation harness, the elicitation budget, the sampled population, and contamination status. Leaderboards publish the model and the score, so capability and leakage stay observationally equivalent. Existing taxonomies classify contamination for automated detection, not the question a reporter faces at publication: given the mitigations already applied, which validity threats remain open? We introduce a taxonomy organized by the mitigation each type defeats -- direct, derivative, temporal, distributional, and acquired -- spanning training-time and evaluation-time leakage. Holding out a private test set closes the first alone. The fifth is acquired during the evaluation itself; because it is a property of one run, it must be recorded with the reported score rather than with the benchmark release. We operationalize it as a four-field disclosure protocol in which "unknown" is a valid entry, released under CC BY 4.0 with a JSON Schema, a validator, and worked examples. Two coders external to the design team applied a pre-registered instrument to 41 documents. Per-variable linear-weighted $\kappa$ runs from 0.00 to 0.35 (median 0.21) over 29 main-pass documents against a single-coder test-retest ceiling of 0.84, collapsing under the class skew the registration anticipated; pooling raises it to 0.46 through chance correction rather than better agreement. Two variables fall below the prevalence-robust threshold registered in advance: strata reporting and the acquired type introduced here. Disagreement concentrates on when a variable applies rather than on what a document states. Elicitation budgets are reported in 13% of documents, and no document addresses all five types. The contribution is the taxonomy, the score-side artifact that follows from it, and a pre-registered measurement of instrument reliability and current disclosure.

papers.title: Exact dynamics of spinning particles and the spin wall in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.abstract: The motion of a spinning test body is governed by the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon equations and deviates from geodesics already at first order in the spin. Most studies of this problem truncate the dynamics at linear order; here we solve the equatorial, spin-aligned problem in Schwarzschild spacetime at all orders in the spin under the Tulczyjew--Dixon condition. Eliminating the four-velocity casts the system into a closed algebraic form and reduces the motion to a single first-order radial equation. Keeping track of both kinematical masses, the norm of the four-momentum and its projection on the velocity, we find that the representative worldline ceases to be timelike on a surface in the space of radius, spin and angular momentum. We call this surface the spin wall. It bounds the radii accessible to a spinning body and is present for every nonvanishing value of the momentum's angular component; only for the purely radial family does it collapse, and that family moves on a geodesic. Its position follows in closed form and may lie inside the horizon, enclose it, or reach the exterior, the last possibility arising already at small spin. We also examine how far the pole--dipole truncation remains under control where the wall is accessible. Within that regime we determine the circular orbits and their stability, the spin dependence of the marginally stable orbit, and the perihelion advance beyond first order in the spin.

papers.title: Response-guided knockoffs for prespecified directional FDR control in linear models
papers.abstract: Conventional false discovery rate (FDR) control limits the expected proportion of selected features that are unrelated to the response. Directional FDR extends this criterion to also account for incorrect sign estimates. In some applications, however, discoveries are sought only in a direction specified in advance. We therefore introduce the prespecified directional FDR, which counts as errors both null effects and effects opposite to the target direction in context of the fixed-design Gaussian linear model with unknown noise variance. A straightforward adaptation of the knockoff filter provides prespecified directional FDR control. To improve power, we develop the response-guided knockoff filter, which uses a noise-perturbed response to guide knockoff construction in favour of features likely to have the target sign, while retaining finite-sample prespecified directional FDR control. Notably, our improved filter maintains this guarantee with a sample size $n>p+2$ in contrast to standard constructions that require $n\geq2p$. Simulations across a range of settings demonstrate power gains of the response-guided knockoff filter. An application to HIV drug-resistance data illustrates improved recovery of externally annotated resistance-associated mutations.

papers.title: Agentic AI uncovers conserved cross-tissue protein co-abundance programs inaccessible to single-dataset analysis
papers.abstract: Protein co-abundance clusters preserved across tissues can nominate shared disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets, particularly where proteins implicated in organ-confined diseases converge in other tissues. Yet cross-tissue proteomic studies have examined pre-selected tissue pairs, leaving most combinations, and non-obvious relationships among them, unexplored. Exhaustive comparison requires consistently assessing thousands of candidate clusters from hundreds of tissue-pair networks across heterogeneous evidence, a scale beyond manual curation. We present an LLM-agent framework for large-scale, evidence-grounded comparison of tissue-specific protein co-abundance networks. From sample-level proteomic data, it constructs tissue networks, derives conserved clusters for each tissue pair, integrates evidence from expression atlases, interaction and complex databases, pathways, disease associations and the literature, and proposes mechanistic hypotheses in which every conclusion cites its evidence. Applied to all 231 pairs among 22 human tissues and sample groups, it identified 1,825 conserved clusters in 216 tissue pairs. Co-abundance relationships were shared beyond chance in 76% of pairs, including unrelated organs, and shared clusters were only weakly associated with abundance similarity. Clusters were enriched 3.7- to 6.9-fold for known interactions and complex memberships, and 379 of 793 testable clusters replicated in independent CPTAC proteomes. Some clusters pointed to relationships absent from current databases: one shared by liver and bone marrow linked three genes causing inherited white matter disorders, suggesting a common mechanism via the integrated stress response. Conserved co-abundance clusters thus offer a hypothesis-generating resource for studying disease proteins beyond the affected organ. Code: https://github.com/jacob20030316-crypto/Protein_Co_Abundance_Agent

papers.title: PULSAR: Pooled Unified Late-Interaction Search and Retrieval for Enterprise Visual Document RAG
papers.abstract: Institutional investors search visually dense pitch decks, board packs, and diligence materials that change hourly near deal closing. OCR followed by figure verbalisation is costly to refresh at this scale and can lose chart detail. We present PULSAR, a production vision-first retrieval system deployed at Mubadala Investment Company. PULSAR indexes page images with a frozen ColPali-style backbone and uses a pooled two-stage late-interaction index: compact page summaries support initial retrieval, followed by exact MaxSim rescoring over a finer pooled representation. On ViDoRe V3, this design reduces median vector-search latency by 15.1 times against an unpooled configuration with less than 0.01 absolute NDCG@10 and Recall@10 loss; production median vector-search latency is 156 ms. Under concurrent load, the pooled index sustains approximately 88 times higher QPS than an unpooled index. The event-driven ingestion path is estimated to be approximately 20 times cheaper per page than the OCR+verbalisation baseline it replaced. Since March 2026, PULSAR has served 78 thousand documents and approximately 2.4 million pages across more than 3,000 deals. At the production top K, it more than doubles answer-fact recall over the OCR+verbalisation baseline.

papers.title: PIFFLE: Characterizing Foreground Dispersion Measure Contributions Across 4 Decades in Halo Mass in the FRB20230907D Field
papers.abstract: We characterize the foreground environment of FRB20230907D, localized to a galaxy at $z=0.464$, which has an observed dispersion measure of ${\rm DM}_{\rm obs}=1031~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$. At its redshift, FRB20230907D lies above the Macquart relation, the expected relation between cosmological dispersion measure and the source redshift, indicating a substantial excess DM along this line of sight. We use Subaru/PFS and SDSS spectroscopy, published group catalogs, Rubin/LSST imaging, and eROSITA X-ray data to characterize the foreground structures that may account for this excess. A friends-of-friends search identifies a massive foreground system at $z\simeq0.09$ with $M_{\rm vir}\simeq7.7\times10^{14}~M_\odot$, while low redshift catalogs reveal an additional group at $z\simeq0.02565$. Assuming that the halo gas follows a modified-NFW halo density profile, we estimate observer frame contributions of $205^{+30}_{-25}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ and $80^{+60}_{-40}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ from these systems, respectively. After accounting for the remaining foreground and host contributions, we are able to make the first-ever constraints on the dispersion measure of a closely-intersected $M_*\approx 10^8\,M_\odot$ dwarf galaxy: ${\rm DM}_{\rm UGC7596}=58^{+53}_{-40}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ at $b_\perp \approx 0.03\,R_{\rm vir}$, which is consistent with hydrodynamical predictions for low mass halos. This highlights the enhancement of dense foreground spectroscopy and multi-wavelength data toward the interpretation of FRB dispersion measures.

papers.title: Selfless Reduced Crossed Product $C^{*}$-Algebras Arising from Almost Periodic Actions
papers.abstract: We prove that the reduced crossed product arising from an almost periodic action of an infinite countable discrete group on a unital, separable $C^*$-algebra is selfless whenever the crossed product is simple and monotracial and the group admits a topologically free extreme boundary action. We also give an alternative proof of a special case of a result of Gao, Junge, Kunnawalkam Elayavalli, Patchell, and Robert: the direct product of an exact $C^*$-simple group and a $C^*$-selfless group is $C^*$-selfless.

papers.title: Sharp Minimax Regret for Infinite-Memory Logistic Prediction
papers.abstract: We study sequential prediction of binary marks whose log-odds are a linear function of all past inputs. The inputs are independent uniform signs. The coefficient of the input observed $j$ steps earlier is unknown, but its absolute value is at most a known number $r_j$, and $\sum_j r_j\le B$. A learner is judged by its expected cumulative log loss in excess of the loss of the true conditional probabilities. We show that for every such sequence $r$ and every horizon $T$, the minimax value of this regret lies between $c\,\Gamma_T(r)/\max\{1,B^2\}$ and $\frac12\Gamma_T(r)$, where $\Gamma_T(r)=\sum_{j\le T}\log(1+(T-j+1)r_j^2)$ and $c$ is an absolute constant. The term for lag $j$ combines the size bound $r_j$ with the number $T-j+1$ of rounds in which that lag influences a prediction, and no monotonicity or other regularity of $r$ is needed. The upper bound is attained by a Bayesian mixture with independent Gaussian priors. For the lower bound, we apply the van Trees inequality at each prediction step and then bound the expected log-determinant of the random matrix whose rows are the lagged input vectors. We also characterize when $\frac12$ is the exact leading constant: for envelopes with a common bound $B$, possibly changing with $T$, the regret is asymptotic to $\frac12\Gamma_T(r)$ if and only if $\sum_{j\le T}\min\{1,(T-j+1)r_j^2\}=o(\Gamma_T(r))$. This gives, for example, $\log^2(A^2T)/(8\alpha)$ for $r_j=Ae^{-\alpha j}$, whereas for $r_j=Aj^{-s}$ with $s>1$ the regret is of order $T^{1/(2s)}$ and its ratio to $\Gamma_T(r)$ stays below $\frac12$. Finally, for a known horizon, an online Newton predictor with features scaled by $r_j$ attains regret of order $\Gamma_T(r)$ with polynomial computation per round.

papers.title: Exact quantum geometry from sublattice symmetry: Closed-form solution of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model
papers.abstract: Quantum geometry has emerged as a guiding principle across atomic and condensed-matter physics, shaping the topological responses of Bloch bands and the stability of the correlated phases they host. Sublattice symmetry, though common among bipartite lattice models, has not yet been exploited to obtain closed-form quantum geometry in multiband systems. For this purpose, we derive a general expression for the QGT of sublattice-symmetric systems in terms of contributions from the individual sublattice sectors, and show that this symmetry renders the Bloch Hamiltonian of a paradigmatic four-band model, the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model, anti-block-diagonal, analytically yielding the spectrum, eigenstates, and full quantum geometric tensor (QGT), including the Berry curvature and quantum metric, for all four bands. The model, describing charged particles on a two-dimensional square lattice subjected to a uniform magnetic field, has recently been realized experimentally with ultracold atoms, photons, and superconducting circuits. Finally, we evaluate fractional-Chern-insulator stability criteria analytically and quantify the lowest band of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model to be a nearly ideal Chern band. Our approach opens a route for studying also the quantum geometry of other sublattice-symmetric multiband systems.

papers.title: Finding and using interpretable latents in a neutrino foundation model with sparse autoencoders
papers.abstract: We present a first application of sparse-autoencoder-based mechanistic interpretability to particle physics. Studying a neutrino foundation model pretrained on IceCube data and fine-tuned for direction reconstruction, we identify a validated atlas of physical concepts in the model representation, using a strict validation protocol consisting of held-out tests, matched nuisance controls, and replication across independent dictionary trainings. Causal interventions show that the direction head barely draws on this atlas. Motivated by this underused information, we train an uncertainty head on the same event-level representation to predict the model's angular reconstruction error. Unlike the direction head, it depends causally on quality and brightness features from the atlas. These results suggest that mechanistic interpretability can reveal learned latent physics encoded within a model's internal representation and help design downstream tasks that exploit it.

papers.title: A High Performance Partial Wave Analysis Framework for Hadron Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Partial wave analysis (PWA) is a key method in hadron physics for extracting the properties of hadronic resonances. As experimental statistics grow, conventional implementations face severe difficulties in both memory usage and speed. We present \texttt{CTPWA}, a high performance PWA framework based on covariant tensor formalism. This framework adopts extensive precomputation and caching mechanisms, as well as fully GPU-based likelihood computation and minimization. With these optimization, the fitting speed is accelerated by two orders of magnitude relative to autograd-based GPU PWA programs, rendering high-statistics partial-wave analysis feasible at high-precision experiments like BESIII.

papers.title: Giant strongly biconnected components of directed networks: a generating function approach
papers.abstract: Strongly connected components (SCCs) characterize modular structure in directed networks but are fragile to single node failures. We study strongly biconnected components (SBCs), which are the set of nodes in which every node pair remains mutually reachable after the removal of any single node, as a more robust notion of connectivity. Using a generating function formalism, we derive the size of the giant SBC and analyze its percolation behavior under random node and link removal. We show that the giant SBC emerges at the same threshold as the giant SCC but grows more slowly, consistent with previous findings for undirected networks. We also applied our theoretical framework to real-world biological networks including gene regulatory networks and neural connectome. Our framework provides insight into the interplay between connectivity, redundancy, and robustness in complex directed systems.

papers.title: Sieve dimension and search depth for the Erd\H{o}s-Straus conjecture, $n \equiv 1 \pmod{24}$
papers.abstract: For primes $n\equiv1\pmod{24}$, we study the depth of explicit, factorization-free searches for a decomposition of $4/n$ into three positive unit fractions. Let $E_2(N;J)$ be the set of such primes $n\le N$ for which no coprime pair $1\le u,a\le J$ admits a divisor $s\mid an+u$ with $s\equiv-1\pmod{4ua}$. For every fixed $J$, we prove $|E_2(N;J)|\ll_J N/(\log N)^{1+A(J)/2}$, where $A(J)$ counts the coprime pairs in $[1,J]^2$. The proof uses a fixed-point-free involution and identifies the exact dimension of the covering. We also establish a dual Type I divisor criterion and an unconditional obstruction: at the fixed shift $c=7$, both branches of the cofactor criterion fail for $\asymp N/(\log N)^{3/2}$ primes. At growing depth, an exact reciprocal-totient asymptotic with leading constant $9/(2\pi^2)$ improves the explicit large-sieve bounds to $O(N\exp(-0.0942(\log N)^{2/3}))$ at cutoff $p>J^5$, and to $O_\varepsilon(N\exp(-(0.1093-\varepsilon)(\log N)^{2/3}))$ at cutoff $p>J^{4+\varepsilon}$ for fixed sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. Finally, combining a truncated Type I pass with a sparse residual search yields a complete, factorization-free batch decision procedure for all primes in $[N,2N]$, using $O(N^2(\log N)^2\exp(-c_0(\log N)^{2/3}))=o(N^2)$ arithmetic operations for some $c_0>0$. The conjecture itself remains open.

papers.title: Multiscale Quasiparticle Electronic Structure and Excitonic Properties of CdSe Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Quantum confinement in stoichiometric $\mathrm{Cd}_n\mathrm{Se}_n$ nanoclusters dramatically attenuates electronic screening, driving a delicate, size-dependent competition between quasiparticle self-energy corrections ($\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$) and exciton binding energies ($E_b$). Here, we present a $GW$/BSE study across a representative size series ($n = 3, 6, 13, 33$) and leverage it to validate a scalable atomistic tight-binding (TB) framework derived from first principles. Our results demonstrate that 1-2 eV spectral blueshifts previously reported in the literature arise from single-particle $GW$ convergence artifacts rather than deficiencies in the electron--hole kernels. We show that the near-perfect cancellation between $\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$ and $E_b$ breaks down as cluster volume increases, driven by the rapid onset of dielectric screening attenuating $E_b$ faster than $\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$ and leading to a pronounced divergence from mean-field predictions. Spatial inverse participation ratio analysis of the electronic structure reveals that optical suppression of fundamental pre-peaks stems from a severe spatial mismatch between localized valence orbitals and delocalized conduction states. Finally, we demonstrate that the confinement-induced scaling of the quasiparticle gap and the optical onset is accurately reproduced by a scissor-corrected, DFT-parameterized TB model. As such, this work provides a quantitative multiscale roadmap for embedding effective many-body effects kernels into computationally efficient models, enabling reliable optical predictions for realistic semiconducting nanostructures containing up to thousands of atoms.

papers.title: ASKAP discovery of a pair of large radio bubbles: on the origin of odd radio circles
papers.abstract: We report the serendipitous discovery of a large, low-surface-brightness radio bubble in 944 MHz continuum data from the ASKAP Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey. The structure, centred on the elliptical galaxy LEDA 217397 at a redshift of $z=0.040$, spans $\sim$8.4 arcmin, corresponding to a projected diameter of $\sim$399 kpc, and consists of two partly overlapping shells both with radii of $\sim$114 kpc. The integrated flux density of the bubble is $56.8\pm2.9$ mJy at 944 MHz, implying a rest-frame 1.4 GHz luminosity of $\sim$ $1.4\times10^{23}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Combining the EMU measurement with MWA GLEAM-X data at 88--185 MHz, we derive a steep integrated spectral index of $\alpha=-1.04\pm0.04$, and a two-frequency spectral-index map suggesting a possible exterior flattening. Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) fitting indicates a massive ($\log M_{\ast}/M\odot = 10.97\pm0.09$), quiescent (SFR=$0.025\pm0.083\,M\odot$ yr$^{-1}$) early-type host with no mid-infrared AGN signature and no overdense environment. We compare the bubble with odd radio circles (ORCs) and large radio shells, and discuss three scenarios for its origin: a starburst-driven wind, a merger-driven shock, and AGN jet-inflated bubbles. The starburst wind is disfavoured on energetic grounds ($\gtrsim$$10^{59}$ erg required versus $\sim$$10^{8}$ yr electron lifetimes), and neither a halo-scale merger shock nor a spherical nuclear blast wave can explain the unusually regular, double-shell geometry; a bipolar nuclear outburst -- a relic AGN jet episode, possibly triggered by a supermassive-black-hole merger -- provides the most natural explanation, with later shocks possibly re-energising the plasma. Deeper broad-band radio, polarimetric, spectroscopic and X-ray observations are needed to confirm its nature.

papers.title: TailSieve: Partial-Rollout-Guided Tail Routing for LLM Rollouts
papers.abstract: Large-scale rollouts have become a core component of modern LLM systems, spanning reinforcement learning (RL) post-training, on-policy distillation, and sampling-heavy evaluation. Unlike online serving, which typically targets request-level latency and throughput, synchronous rollouts must collect a complete batch before proceeding. A few long-tail generations can therefore dominate an entire rollout step, and uniform routing can slow these generations further by placing them in high-concurrency decoding batches. We present TailSieve, a partial-rollout-guided framework that jointly controls tail routing and replica allocation. Motivated by the observed persistence of prompt-level tail tendencies across policy updates, TailSieve uses partial-rollout completion status as a training-free signal for identifying candidate tail groups. Selected prompts are combined with newly sampled prompts, and all responses are generated from scratch under the current policy. A hierarchical controller uses response-work history and a serving model: a fast inner loop adjusts the number of isolated groups to balance completion times, while a slower outer loop adapts how many replicas serve these groups. The resulting low-concurrency execution also enables route-specialized speculative decoding with MTP or DFlash. Across the evaluated configurations, TailSieve achieves up to $1.67\times$ speedup with routing alone and $2.59\times$ with routing and speculation combined, both over uniform group routing.

papers.title: Guidance for Prior Change via Density Ratio Estimation
papers.abstract: Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) serves as a vital framework for parameter inference in scientific fields where simulators involve intractable likelihoods, yet while amortized generative models offer rapid posterior estimation, they are often restricted by the specific priors used during training, thereby limiting their flexibility as prior knowledge evolves. To address this prior dependency, PriorGuide was introduced as an inference-time guidance method, but due to its intractable formulation, it relies on Gaussian approximations of the reverse transition kernel and Gaussian mixture model fitting for the prior ratio, both of which introduce systematic bias. Motivated by these limitations, we propose an unbiased test-time guidance framework that leverages Density Ratio Estimation (DRE) to learn a score guidance term, effectively decoupling the inference process from the prior training. Moreover, our framework remains agnostic to the specific density ratio estimators, making it a general and flexible framework for handling prior changes. Experimental results across multiple tasks demonstrate that our method matches or outperforms PriorGuide on C2ST and MMD in most tasks while maintaining robustness even under limited overlap between the training and target priors. Furthermore, we apply our method to Bayesian updating for parameter inference from planetary light-curve data, where it also demonstrates strong effectiveness and robustness. Code is available at https://github.com/a-chenchen/dre-based-prior-guidance .

papers.title: A Note on a High-Energy Limit of Gravitational Perturbation Theory
papers.abstract: The post-Minkowskian expansion of general relativity expands the metric in Newton's constant G around flat space-time, but much effort currently focuses on ways to extend its range of applicability by summing the perturbative series to all orders. A regime of particular interest is a specific high-energy limit where a formula derived recently provides the momentum kick of binary scattering problem to all orders, and even suggests an approach towards strong coupling. We show that this is an asymptotic expansion. Although the series diverges we give evidence that it is Borel summable, and the full function in integral form is finite. As a by-product we determine the transcendentality properties of the coefficients in the expanded expression.

papers.title: Kerr Quasinormal Modes without Variable Separation: A Two-Dimensional Hyperboloidal Teukolsky Solver with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We use physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to solve the gravitational quasinormal-mode (QNM) eigenvalue problem for Kerr spacetime directly in the two-dimensional hyperboloidal formulation of the Teukolsky equation. This formulation does not require separation of variables and thus retains the coupled radial--angular structure. Such a scheme provides a prototype for calculating the QNMs of beyond-Kerr black holes for which the perturbation equations are non-separable. Sequences with increasing angular momentum are constructed, reaching close to the extremal limit. We focus on the fundamental modes $(\ell,m,n)=(2,0,0)$, $(2,1,0)$, $(2,2,0)$, $(3,3,0)$ and $(4,4,0)$, together with the first two overtones $(2,2,1)$ and $(2,2,2)$. After training, the frequency at every spin is refined by solving the discretized equation for it, so that it depends much less on where the stochastic training happens to stop. Comparison with continued-fraction values shows that every reported real and imaginary frequency component of the production network remains below $0.23\%$ error, with a median deviation of $2\times10^{-4}\%$. For the fundamental modes, both components agree within about $10^{-3}\%$ up to $a/M=0.97$, and the real parts within $5\times10^{-4}\%$ at every spin. Sub-percent accuracy is maintained in the near-extremal regime, where the damping rate becomes small and the modes are longest-lived; there the damping errors grow, and the largest, $0.23\%$, belongs to the $(2,2,1)$ overtone. The results establish a non-spectral numerical route to multidimensional black-hole perturbation eigenproblems which does not match the substantially higher precision of dedicated Kerr solvers but offers greater flexibility and requires less analytical pre-processing. The proposed approach is designed to be applicable to other backgrounds whose perturbation equations do not separate.

papers.title: Discretizing Continuous Time Series for Imputation with Masked Diffusion Training
papers.abstract: Time series imputation is a crucial area for reliable time series analysis, yet it remains challenging due to the complex temporal dynamics and noise of real-world data. Existing approaches, however, exhibit two limitations: missing and observed values are embedded within the same representation space without explicit structural separation, and continuous diffusion-based methods recover the missing values only through many iterative denoising steps rather than by predicting them directly. To address these, we propose the Masked Diffusion Time-series Imputation Model (MDTIM), which leverages the training paradigm of masked diffusion model for imputation tasks. The [MASK] token is structurally orthogonal to valid observations, and because the corrupted state is the partially observed series itself, the model is trained to predict the missing values directly from the observed ones, naturally aligning both the representation and the learning objective with the imputation task. To bridge the gap between discrete masked diffusion and the continuous, ordinal nature of time series, we further introduce Stochastic Discretization, which maps continuous values to ordinal-aware tokens while preserving continuous dynamics. Our experiments on diverse benchmarks confirm that MDTIM achieves superior robustness and scalability, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art deterministic and generative baselines across various missing scenarios. Code and project page are available at https://dongbeank.github.io/MDTIM/.

papers.title: Monroe: A Molecular Foundation Model for In-Context Probabilistic Inference
papers.abstract: Bioassay activity prediction is often data-limited because drug-discovery datasets rely on time-consuming and expensive wet-lab experiments for data generation and evaluation. This challenge has inspired recent research into molecular foundation models (MFMs), which aim to encode general-purpose chemical knowledge into molecular representations that generalize well in data-constrained scenarios. This paper presents Monroe, a new MFM with several innovations over the existing state of the art: increased scale allowing pre-training on over 81 million molecules from the PM6 quantum chemistry dataset; improved graph representation of stereochemistry; improved training losses including conformer denoising and embedding decorrelation; improved multi-task learning; and the use of a prior-data-fitted model (TabPFNv3) for downstream in-context prediction. Our evaluations use a principled pairwise comparison framework that measures statistically significant performance differences. Across established Polaris benchmarks, Monroe matches or exceeds existing MFMs, while on activity cliff benchmarks, designed to assess utility for molecular discovery, it achieves significant improvements over prior methods. Finally, ablation and transfer experiments show that PFN-based downstream predictors also substantially improve two leading existing models, MiniMol and CheMeleon, yielding new state-of-the-art variants we call MiniMol_PFN and CheMeleon_PFN, suggesting that our downstream adaptation strategy generalizes beyond Monroe. Source code is at github.com/blazejba/Monroe

papers.title: Spanning $H$-subdivisions with Prescribed Path Lengths
papers.abstract: We study spanning $H$-subdivisions in dense graphs where the length of every subdivision path is prescribed in advance. This problem is motivated in part by a question of Pavez-Sign\'e [Combin. Probab. Comput. 33 (2024), 121--128], who asked whether the subdivision paths in a spanning $H$-subdivision can be required to have similar lengths. Let $h\ge3$ be an integer and let $0<\beta\ll\alpha\ll1/h$. We prove that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge n/2+\lfloor h/3\rfloor$ has the following property. For every graph $H$ with $h$ edges and no isolated vertices, write $E(H)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_h\}$, and every choice of integers $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_h\ge4$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^h\ell_i=n-|V(H)|+h$ and $\sum_{\ell_i<\alpha n}\ell_i\le\beta n$, the graph $G$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision in which the $i$th edge of $H$ is replaced by a path of length exactly $\ell_i$. We also give a family of examples showing that a linear additive term in $h$ is necessary in general.

papers.title: MEDR: Query-Independent Frame Selection via Multi-Signal Event Modeling and Dynamic Rescoring
papers.abstract: Frame selection is a fundamental component of multimodal large language models, enabling long videos to be processed under limited visual-token and computational budgets. Uniform sampling preserves temporal coverage but may miss informative content that appears only briefly. To alleviate this limitation, query-dependent methods can retrieve question-relevant frames. However, because the selected frames depend on the current question, the same visual input cannot be directly shared across different questions, and frame selection must be repeated in multi-turn video dialogue. This motivates us to seek a query-independent frame selection method that preserves the reusability of a fixed visual input while improving the coverage of informative events beyond uniform sampling. We propose Multi-Signal Event Modeling and Dynamic Rescoring (MEDR), a training-free and query-independent frame selection method. Multi-Signal Event Modeling organizes complementary visual, motion, and text signals into signal-specific temporal events. Dynamic Rescoring then iteratively reevaluates each candidate relative to the current selected set, updating its score according to frame-level signal strength, additional event coverage, and balanced temporal coverage. The resulting fixed frame set is constructed without observing the query and can be reused across different questions. Experiments on Video-MME and LongVideoBench demonstrate that MEDR achieves competitive performance across two video MLLMs. Under the 64-frame budget, MEDR improves Video-MME accuracy over the strongest evaluated query-independent baseline by 1.33-1.78 percentage points. We further evaluate the reuse of a fixed frame set in multi-question video dialogue.

papers.title: Hidden transverse-flow topology in partially coherent structured light
papers.abstract: Partial coherence is commonly viewed as a mechanism that reduces contrast or smooths intensity structure. Here we show that it can also encode hidden transverse-flow topology. Starting from the cross-spectral density, we formulate a generalized transverse flux, an effective velocity field, and the associated flux trajectories for quasi-monochromatic partially coherent paraxial beams. This construction converts two-point correlation phases into local transport information and reduces to the usual coherent energy-flow picture in the single-mode limit. Because the generalized flux is obtained through a local differential operation on the cross-spectral density, the proposed trajectories are, in principle, reconstructible from sufficiently resolved phase-sensitive measurements of the complex second-order coherence function, subject to the regularization required by numerical differentiation. Two analytical beam families expose this hidden topology. In twisted Gaussian Schell-model beams, a Gaussian intensity hides a distributed rotational flow with nonzero vorticity. In Laguerre-Christoffel-Darboux beams, sources with identical intensity profiles can have different flux topology, producing either spiral or purely radial trajectories. Thus, intensity and coherence magnitude do not exhaust the physical information contained in the cross-spectral density: partial coherence can reorganize the hidden topology of transverse optical transport.

papers.title: From Block Orthogonality to Decidability in Complex-Weighted Counting CSP
papers.abstract: In a landmark JACM paper recognized with the 2021 G\"odel Prize, Cai and Chen established a complexity dichotomy for counting CSPs over arbitrary finite domains with algebraic complex weights. Their tractability criterion consists of three conditions on the infinite family of functions obtained from CSP instances by summing out some variables: the Block Orthogonality and Type Partition conditions, and a Mal'tsev polymorphism condition on support and row-equivalence relations. They left open whether this criterion is decidable from the finite set of constraint functions. We resolve this question by giving a total exact algorithm for every $q$-element domain ($q\ge 1$), with algebraic weights encoded exactly. We also prove that the Block Orthogonality condition implies the other two conditions, reducing the tractability criterion to a single structural property. We obtain similar decidability and structural results for Lin's tractability criterion for $\#\mathrm{CSP}^{d}$, where each variable occurs a multiple of $d$ times. Our method first shows that every failure of Block Orthogonality can be witnessed by a generated function of arity at most $q^2+1$. At each such arity, we reduce checking infinitely many generated functions to finitely many exact algebraic tests, using tensor products and a pinned extension of Young's all-instance isomorphism theorem. For the structural implication, we use powers of generated functions to control complex cancellation and construct functions whose supports encode row equivalence. These constructions yield the Type Partition and Mal'tsev polymorphism conditions.

papers.title: AuditLock: Pre-Specified Verification Audits for Synthetic Tabular Data Releases
papers.abstract: A statistical office with a synthetic version of a protected file must decide whether it may be released for a stated purpose. We study the locked audit, a pre-specified and simultaneous form of the verification servers used in official statistics. Before a protected audit sample is opened, the custodian fixes the use, the candidates, the analyses, a tolerance for each and the schedule. The audit then reports simultaneous finite-sample bounds on paired loss gaps, and a declared negative control must fail. We correct an anytime-valid sequence that an earlier release had implemented with a variance penalty four times too small. Two confirmatory rounds were pre-specified in a hash-locked local ledger and publicly timestamped only after the audits. The control and ideal-generator outcomes were near-certain by design. A Gaussian copula certified in every cell, but only inside the rounding step of the tolerance rule. A second transparent candidate certified once, against a written prediction.
